rule: Legacy caller/provider coupling is migrated incrementally; no authority boundary may be weakened merely to achieve code reuse.

items.problem: Playbook autonomy review owned Teams card rendering and raw Teams gateway HTTP transport.
items.target: Provider-neutral approval workflow plus shared Teams approval-delivery adapter.
items.evidence: playbook_autonomy_review now depends only on ApprovalRequestSender; Teams transport moved to teams_approval_delivery.py

items.problem: Billing-audit maintenance owns raw Teams gateway HTTP notification transport.
items.target: Reuse canonical Teams message delivery with an exact workload/recipient policy or another shared communication capability contract.
items.blocker: communication.teams.message.send currently has owner-approval semantics that do not match scheduled billing notifications; do not weaken that authority merely to migrate.

items.problem: Autonomous completion notifications define a second Teams send capability/provider and own raw Teams gateway transport.
items.target: One shared Teams message implementation with caller-specific exact authority/grant policy and fixed-recipient constraints where required.
items.blocker: Must preserve autonomous fixed-recipient and event-type constraints while removing duplicate transport.

items.problem: Autonomous repair maintenance reads GitHub pull requests and commits through raw GitHub HTTP.
items.target: Canonical source/repository pull-request and commit read capabilities.
items.blocker: No active canonical repository-source read capability is currently available for this maintenance path.

items.problem: Workflow imported provider-neutral approval contracts from the connector package.
items.evidence: workflow now imports orchestrator.approval_requests; connector path is compatibility-only

next_migration_rule: Prefer the highest-impact item whose canonical target can be implemented without broadening authority, client scope, provider permission, or disruption.
